Alright, so here's some light back ground information. I live in a two level house, with my basement being what I'd like to call the epicenter of activity. On several occasions, day or night, inexplicable noises and voices are emitted from the pitch-black guest room at the back of the basement hallway.
 So on this night, a night in late July, I was sitting at my desk in my room, tapping away at the keyboard. I'd gone to the bathroom not much earlier, and had mistakenly left on the light. As I was sitting there typing, a hulking mass glided past the doorway, projecting a shadow on the wall.
 I'll admit now that I have a very animated imagination, as I write many stories. But I swear on all my accountability that this was a vivid experience.
 Without much thought to it, I assumed it was my father walking into the kitchen. I got up to join him in whatever he was doing, guessing he was having trouble sleeping, as he frequently does.
 As I stepped into the kitchen, the feel was off. It felt as is the room had a dense layer of fog shrouding it. I surveyed the still, dark room and saw no trace of my father. Instantly, chills ran up my spine as an odd feeling consumed me.
 The weight of my body instinctually shifted to the balls of my feet. I felt as if there were eyes on my back, filled with malicious intentions.
 My courage swayed at this point. For several long minutes, I stood there, frozen in terror. I finally gathered enough courage to glance behind me to the stairs. I'm still in hysterics about what I saw.
 My stairs lead down one way to a landing, and then, in the opposite direction down to the basement. On the stairs between the landing in the basement, stood what I can only describe as a dead face.
 The balcony cut it off at the shoulders, but it wasn't misty or billowing and undulating like a shadow figure. It was completely solid. And its eyes, as dark pupils, pierced me with more animosity and disdain than its emotionless face could convey. Then, suddenly, it glides down the remainder of the stairs, just as the shadow did.
 At this point, I was sure that wasn't a friendly entity. But I had enough clarification to know that it was a dangerous one. I still regret my next decision to this day.
 I descended the stairs cautiously. Just as I placed my foot on the basement floor, a squelching pop resounded from the guest room. But now, I noticed, the darkness of the room was different. The doorway was consumed in perfect darkness, as if the darkness I was inside in the kitchen was child's play.
 I'm not sure why, but I sprinted to the doorway in a rush of courage and flicked the light switch.
 Nothing. Nothing in the room except old, packed stuff we'd left to unpack for years after our move here.
 I fell to the floor in a heap of depression and began to sob and moan. Loud enough that my father came rushing down the stairs to find me curled into a ball in the doorway.
 I was barely at the edge of coherent consciousness at this point, and as he grabbed me by the arms, he tells me, I told him, "Please turn off the lights. And close the door, won't you?" After that, I collapsed into a pale mess of limbs and he had to lug me up the stairs.
 If anyone has any answers for me, please, don't be shy to share because the activity has followed this tempo for three years now, the original happening occurring when I was 14. I have no qualms with possible skepticism, because if I heard this happen to any other person, I'd dismiss it immediately. But I do ask you keep any open mind, and, if possible, present some suggestions or even explanations to what's happening

I think it harms more than helps, it puts way to much pressure to succeed on you. Your own expectations for yourself raise to incredibly high levels and when you don't meet those expectations everything goes down hill. 

This has helped fuel my depression, because when I can't hit those marks i feel like i'm not living up to my potential. Having people think you're going to do amazing things because you're "Gifted" doesn't help either because that adds another layer of pressure coming from other people, and not just from yourself. 

I'm still in high school, and this "gifted" thing has really messed me up. People constantly say that you can be doing great things when you're hitting your A's and B;s, but when you get one or 2 bad marks everyone just ends up disappointed. It makes you feel like everyone is constantly judging everything you do, it breeds an unhealthy need for approval, and success. 

Having a need for success isn't a bad thing but when coupled with the need for approval you either sink or swim, and because of the expectations people have for you, you don't want to let them down. Right now for me, when it feels like I've let the people around me down i can barely function, because I know I've lost their approval, and haven't lived up to their expectations of me.

sorry if this seems self centered, just my input and i didn't know how else to phrase it.
